A fantasy romance based on Neil Gaiman and Charles Vess' Vertigo miniseries.

comics.ord: Introduces Barry Allen, generally considered the start of the Silver Age.
comics.blurb: Barry Allen becomes the second Flash, kicking off DC's Silver Age revival of its heroes.

comics.ord: The formation of the modern Justice League.

comics.ord: Introduces the New Gods and Darkseid into the DC Universe.

comics.blurb: Barry Allen wakes in an altered timeline, and undoing it reshapes the entire DC Universe.

comics.ord: The flagship launch title of the New 52 relaunch.
comics.blurb: Geoff Johns and Jim Lee retell the League's formation for DC's rebooted continuity.

comics.t: Batman (Snyder run): Court of Owls / Death of the Family / Zero Year / Endgame
comics.ord: The defining New 52 Batman run, from a secret society to a reworked origin (Zero Year).
comics.blurb: Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo's acclaimed run, widely considered the New 52's standout Bat-era.

comics.ord: A reworked, younger and more rebellious early Superman.
comics.blurb: Grant Morrison revisits Superman's earliest days with a rougher, more populist edge.

comics.ord: A mythology-heavy reboot leaning into the Greek gods as active, dangerous family.
comics.blurb: Brian Azzarello and Cliff Chiang reframe Diana's world as a blood-soaked divine soap opera.

comics.ord: A standalone, self-contained continuity separate from the mainline New 52.
comics.blurb: Geoff Johns reimagines a younger, more fallible Batman's origin from scratch.

comics.ord: Restores legacy and history erased by the New 52; the gateway into the Rebirth era.
comics.blurb: Wally West re-emerges to restore lost history — and to warn that Doctor Manhattan is behind it.

comics.t: Batman (Tom King run): I Am Gotham / War of Jokes and Riddles / City of Bane
comics.ord: Builds toward a (ultimately unconsummated) wedding to Catwoman, then Bane's takeover of Gotham.
comics.blurb: A psychologically dense run exploring Bruce Wayne's relationships and his breaking point.

comics.ord: Introduces Jon Kent, Clark and Lois's son, as a central family dynamic.
comics.blurb: Tomasi and Gleason ground Superman in fatherhood alongside young son Jon.

comics.ord: Joshua Williamson's long Flash run establishing Force-related mythology (Speed Force, Still Force, etc).
comics.blurb: Barry Allen mentors a new generation of speedsters while confronting his father-figure, Zoom.

comics.ord: A direct sequel to Watchmen, formally merging its characters into DCU continuity.
comics.blurb: Geoff Johns brings Doctor Manhattan and Ozymandias into the mainstream DC Universe.

comics.ord: Follows Dark Nights: Death Metal; reopens and reorganizes the multiverse again.
comics.blurb: A soft-relaunch event restoring an open, playground multiverse after years of restriction.

comics.ord: Leads directly into the Dawn of DC branding and line-wide relaunch.
comics.blurb: With the Justice League dead, a new generation of heroes must hold the multiverse together.

comics.ord: Covers Fear State and Joker War's aftermath into the Dawn of DC relaunch.
comics.blurb: Gotham fractures under Ghost-Maker, Scarecrow's Fear State, and a rebuilt Batman Family.

comics.ord: Not connected to main continuity — a from-scratch alternate reality launched alongside Absolute Superman and Absolute Wonder Woman.
comics.blurb: Scott Snyder reimagines a rawer, working-class Bruce Wayne in a brand-new alternate universe line.

comics.ord: Part of the same new Absolute Universe imprint as Absolute Batman.
comics.blurb: A version of Superman who grew up without the Kents' wealth of the mainline continuity.

comics.ord: Part of the Absolute Universe imprint.
comics.blurb: A darker, more mythic reimagining of Diana's origins outside the mainline DCU.

comics.ord: Standalone continuity; spawned its own sequel line (Curse of the White Knight, etc).
comics.blurb: The Joker is cured of his insanity and turns his intellect toward exposing Batman as the true menace.

comics.ord: Loosely canon-adjacent; answers a long-running fan theory about multiple Jokers.
comics.blurb: Geoff Johns and Jason Fabok explore the idea that three different men have worn the Joker identity.

comics.ord: Ambiguous continuity placement; part of a loose Black Label trilogy with Superman and Wonder Woman entries.
comics.blurb: A surreal murder mystery over the Joker's death, painted by Lee Bermejo.

comics.ord: Standalone; not connected to main continuity.
comics.blurb: A Cold War-era Elseworlds reimagining the Justice League's formative years against real 1970s history.

comics.ord: Standalone myth-retelling; not connected to main continuity.
comics.blurb: Kelly Sue DeConnick reframes the Amazons' founding myth with a harder, more brutal edge.

comics.ord: Direct tie-in prequel/companion to the fighting game's alternate timeline.
comics.blurb: Chronicles Superman's fall into tyranny between the game's story beats.

comics.ord: Self-contained; unconnected to the DCU.
comics.blurb: Garth Ennis's blasphemous road-trip saga about a preacher possessed by a being born of an angel and a demon.

comics.ord: Self-contained; unconnected to the DCU.
comics.blurb: Fairy-tale characters live in exile in modern New York after being driven from their homelands.
